cards.title: The bipolar screen was measured against the full-mania yardstick
cards.detail: Asked why bipolar disorder was ruled out, the witness described mania: seven days of euphoria with very high energy, plus grandiosity, major risk-taking and a truly reduced need for sleep. The public sources below say hypomania, the lower bar seen in bipolar II, needs about four days, is less severe, and can present as irritable rather than euphoric mood. They also say antidepressants are not used alone when bipolar disorder is present. On September 15 the witness describes asking about a period of excessive energy and euphoria and 'leaving it there.' This card does not say the patient had hypomania; that is a clinical question. It records which yardstick the screen used. Neither source addresses postpartum presentations.

sources.span: seven days of continued euphoria with very high energy levels
it was not deemed that she had bipolar disorder
I might leave it there and then follow up with some of the other symptoms

references.label: NIMH: Bipolar disorder
references.note: Mania lasts at least 7 days; hypomania is less severe and interferes less with daily life; antidepressants are not used alone.

references.label: Cleveland Clinic: Hypomania
references.note: Hypomania lasts at least 4 days in a row, is shorter and less severe than mania, can include irritable mood, and usually does not need hospital care.

cards.title: The last antidepressant trial began eight days before January 24
cards.detail: Amitriptyline 10 mg, the lowest dose, was started on January 16 and filled the same day. The NHS gives 2 to 4 weeks for first improvement and 4 to 6 for full effect. The FDA label says anyone starting an antidepressant should be closely monitored for clinical worsening and unusual changes in behavior, especially early on and at dose changes, and that monitoring should include daily observation by family or caregivers. It also says patients should be screened for bipolar disorder before an antidepressant is started, and that a causal link between early agitation or insomnia and worsening has not been established. This card does not say the drug caused anything; that needs evidence specific to her and expert review. It records the timing and what the label expects around it.

sources.span: We did go ahead and decide to try the amitriptyline
the prescription was filled on that same day, January 16th, 2023
she had started the amitriptyline

references.label: NHS: About amitriptyline for depression
references.note: May start to feel better after 2 to 4 weeks; can take 4 to 6 weeks to work fully.

references.label: NHS: How and when to take amitriptyline
references.note: Usual adult dose is 50 mg a day; some people start on 10 to 25 mg to reduce side effects, then increase gradually.

references.label: FDA label: amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets (2016)
references.note: Monitor for clinical worsening, suicidality and unusual behavior early and at dose changes, including daily family observation; screen for bipolar disorder first; causal link to early symptoms not established; no increased suicidality signal in adults over 24 in short-term trials.

questions.text: Who was the accountable post-McLean clinician or team?
Who received and reviewed the complete inpatient record, and who reconciled every medication actually being taken?
Which clinicians communicated directly with one another, on what dates?
Who was monitoring longitudinal improvement rather than relying on whether SI/HI was denied in a given visit?
Was PHP or IOP merely recommended, or were enrollment, attendance, refusal or waitlist status confirmed?
Who collected collateral from family, and was there a supervision or child-safety plan during medication changes?
